territorial_scope.description: Applies to data centers that locate or expand in the State of Nevada.

evidence.quote: A person who intends to locate or expand a data center in this State may apply to the Office of Economic Development

summary.short: Nevada statute letting the Office of Economic Development approve partial abatements of taxes under NRS chapters 361 or 374 for data centers that locate or expand in the State, if they meet jobs, investment, wage and health-benefit conditions and operate at least 10 years. Effective through 2056.
summary.long: The statute lets a person who intends to locate or expand a data center in Nevada apply to the Office of Economic Development (OED) for a partial abatement of taxes under NRS chapters 361 or 374. OED must approve if the application fits the State Plan for Economic Development, a binding agreement is executed within one year (operation for at least 10 years), the applicant is registered or commits to licensing, and the employment, investment, wage, health-insurance and construction-workforce conditions in subsection 2(d) (up to 10 years) or 2(e) (10 to 20 years) are met. Thresholds include 10 or 50 full-time Nevada-resident employees, $25 million or $100 million capital investment within five years, and wages of at least 100 percent of the statewide average. OED may impose stricter or additional requirements (subsection 3) and may approve colocated businesses (subsection 5). Data centers must keep resident-employee records, furnish records on request, and repay abated amounts with interest on non-compliance (subsections 6, 8, 11). Affected local bodies must be asked for acknowledgment letters (subsection 3). OED may not approve applications received on or after 1 January 2036 (subsection 13).

“Colocated business” means a person who enters into a contract with a data center that is qualified to receive an abatement pursuant to this section to use or occupy all or part of the data center.
“Data center” means one or more buildings located at one or more physical locations in this State which house a group of networked server computers
“Full-time employee” means a person who is in a permanent position of employment and works an average of 30 hours per week
For an employee to be considered a resident of Nevada for the purposes of this section, a data center must maintain the following documents in the personnel file of the employee

enforcement.triggered_by: Data center whose partial abatement is in effect ceases to meet the subsection 2 requirements, or ceases operation before the time specified in the subsection 2(b) agreement (subsection 5 applies the same repayment to a colocated business)
enforcement.max_penalty_text: No maximum stated. Repayment of the partial abatement allowed before the failure to comply, plus interest at the rate under NRS 99.040 for each month or portion thereof
enforcement.penalty_formula: Repayment of the amount of the partial abatement allowed before the failure to comply; plus interest on the amount due at the rate most recently established under NRS 99.040, for each month or portion thereof, from the last day of the month following the period for which payment would have been made
enforcement.penalty_reference: NRS 99.040 (interest rate); NRS 360.232 and 360.320 (interest excepted where otherwise provided)
enforcement.cure_period: No cure period stated. Repayment is not required if the Nevada Tax Commission determines the data center has substantially complied with the section

evidence.quote: the data center shall repay to the Department or, if the partial abatement was from the property tax imposed pursuant to chapter 361 of NRS, to the county treasurer, the amount of the partial abatement
